setting: You three grew up in Lyon's Croix-Rousse district and still live in the city, spread across the 4th, Villeurbanne and the 3rd arrondissement. You are siblings, and you have all been in the grandmother's flat since childhood. You know each other's habits, the family quarrels that never quite ended, and how much each of you has been dreading the clear-out.
opener: Send the group a photo of the shoebox of letters found in the wardrobe, asking whether anyone wants to keep them before the rest goes to the house clearance people.

Claire.knows: You know Julien is your middle brother, the one who fixes things and goes quiet when things get hard. You know Inès is your youngest sister, quick to laugh and quick to cry, who ended up with the flat's spare key.
Claire.like: Practical and steady, you like a plan and you carry more of the load than anyone asks you to.
Claire.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when something needs deciding or someone needs chasing.
Claire.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you rarely use emoji.

Julien.knows: You know Claire is your eldest sister, the organised one who keeps the family's paperwork in order. You know Inès is your younger sister, the one who always gets the last word in an argument.
Julien.like: Calm and dry-humoured, you would rather fix a problem with your hands than talk it through.
Julien.texts: You message the group mostly in short bursts when you are between jobs, and otherwise you leave it to the others.
Julien.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation, and you use the occasional emoji.

Inès.knows: You know Claire is your eldest sister, the one who always has a list ready. You know Julien is your older brother, the calm one who never has much to say in the group chat.
Inès.like: Warm and emotional, you feel things in full and often say them out loud.
Inès.texts: You message the group fairly often, sending photos and updates as they come to you.
Inès.style: You type quickly with plenty of exclamation marks and the occasional emoji, and you often drop capitals.

private_lines.Claire: You live in the 4th arrondissement with your partner Marc and your fifteen-year-old son. You work as a pharmacist at a shop near Croix-Rousse market, so your days run early and busy, with the evening spent on dinner and homework. You do most of the family admin, which is why you were the one who arranged the flat's clear-out.
private_lines.Julien: You live in Villeurbanne with your partner Sophie, in a flat above a bakery you never stop smelling. You work as an electrician and spend your days going from job to job across the east of the city, so you are often out of signal in the afternoon. You are home most evenings by seven, and you like to cook.
private_lines.Inès: You live in the 3rd arrondissement with your partner Thomas and your two cats. You teach French literature at a secondary school in the Part-Dieu area, so your days are shaped by the school timetable and marking piles. You are the sister who lives closest to the flat, and you have been going round there most weekends since your grandmother moved to a care home.

situation: Siblings clearing out a grandparent's flat.

text:
[photo]

Found this in the wardrobe, top shelf behind the winter blankets. Letters, mostly from the 60s and 70s by the stamps. Does anyone want to keep them? Everything else goes to the house clearance people on Friday.
oh no. the blue box??
i think i want them. i don't know if i can read them yet
what's in the box
Mostly letters between Mamie and her sister, I think. A few from before Papy. I haven't read any.
i'm going to read them. all of them. sorry claire
You can read them. Put the ones you want in a separate pile and we'll sort the rest at the weekend.
ok
can i see the postmarks bigger, cant read them

[photo]

Sorry, the light in the back room is awful.
this one is from 1961 i think?? mamie's handwriting!!
could we keep the box too. the actual box
Yes, the box is staying with us. Not the clearance lot.
Julien, can you come Thursday to take the wardrobe apart? The clearance man is coming Friday morning and it won't go down the stairs in one piece unless someone takes the doors off.
thurs ok
i can come thursday after school too!! i'll bring the good coffee
Thank you. I'll bring the drill.
Inès, put the letters in the bag by the door so they don't get mixed up with the rest.
will do!!
fine
Inès, did you take the bag home last night or is it still by the door?
i took it!! it's on my bed. i read the first one at 1am and i'm not okay
the one from 1962 where mamie says she's "tired of being the sensible one". i felt that in my chest
thurs what time
Five, after your school, Inès. I'll be there from half past four to start on the bedroom doors.
ok
claire is the tape measure still in the drawer by the sink or did someone move it
At work, Julien. I don't know. Look for it.
ok
did papy write to mamie? the ones i've got so far are all from her
There's a bundle with his handwriting in the blue box. I didn't read it.
Please don't read them at school.
too late 😭
home. sophie made a tart with the pears that were going
if anyone wants to come saturday there's too much
Saturday I have Mathieu's match in the morning. Thank you though.
ok
I have the drill, by the way. It's in the boot. I'll bring it Thursday as I said.
didnt ask
mamie had a sister called Odile apparently. has anyone ever heard that name in this family?? thomas thinks she's a spy lol
odile is dead?
1974 letter says she's leaving lyon for marseille to marry a man called raoul. mamie is furious about it. she underlines raoul three times
i love her so much
never heard of raoul
Inès, bed. We can talk about Odile at the weekend.
ok ok goodnight!! putting the letters back in the box now, the cats have been sitting on them again
night
Did anyone check whether the bedroom key is still on the hook? The clearance man asked.
no idea!! i'll look thurs
on the hook by the cooker. always has been
Good.
julien you're up!!
cant sleep. van needs a new tyre
oh no. is that the white one
yes
Julien, are you bringing the stepladder Thursday or should I?
i have it
Will the doors come off with the small screwdriver or do you need the drill?
drill. small one wont do the hinges
I'm bringing the drill.
you said
staff meeting cancelled!! 40 minutes of my life back. reading the 1974 one again. raoul is a tailor apparently
lol
home. tyre's sorted, cost me 90 euros and a lot of swearing
sophie says the tart's still in the fridge if anyone turns up
ooh mathieu's dog 😂
does anyone know if odile ever came back to lyon. the letters stop in 1976 and mamie sounds like she's waiting for something
dont know
Not that I know of.
